title: Student housing proposal at 601 Scottsdale Drive
subtitle: Heritage designations, a letter to the province on heritage registers, a draft approval extension, and the CAO's farewell.
overview: Council held the statutory public meeting on proposed Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments for 601 Scottsdale Drive in Ward 5. The applicant wants to build two 7-storey buildings with 489 residential suites geared to students on the vacant part of the property. Council received the staff report {{vote:m2}}. No decision was made, and staff will bring a recommendation report to a later meeting. No members of the public spoke.

Residents can ask to be added to the interested parties list by emailing planning@guelph.ca. Councillors asked about parking, electric vehicle spaces, bike parking, accessible units and how the building would be limited to University of Guelph students. They also asked that the next report cover the financial implications, including a property tax exemption request for the first phase.

Council also adopted its consent agenda. It included notices of intention to designate five properties under the Ontario Heritage Act, a draft approval extension for 55 and 75 City Fleet Drive, and a letter to the province asking for a five-year extension of the heritage register deadline. The mayor also marked the retirement of Chief Administrative Officer Scott Stewart, who attended his last council meeting.

decisions.detail: Council received the statutory public meeting report on Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments for two 7-storey student residential buildings with 489 suites, with no decision on the applications yet {{vote:m2}}.

Council adopted the consent items, which the mayor read out as notices of intention to designate five properties under the Ontario Heritage Act, a draft approval extension for 55 and 75 City Fleet Drive, and a letter to the premier and minister requesting that the heritage register removal deadline move from January 1, 2025 to January 1, 2030.

debate: Councillors asked why the recommendation says the suites are geared to students and how renting could be limited to University of Guelph students. Staff said the wording reflects a site-specific definition from the first phase and the land lease with the university, and promised clearer wording in the decision report.

One councillor said it matters that the developer is a private company, not the university, because the first phase has a request for a property tax exemption. That councillor asked that the next report include a financial implications section.
A councillor questioned the reduced electric vehicle parking. The applicant's planner said surface spaces could be converted to chargers later if demand grows.

On bike parking, a councillor asked whether about half a space per unit is enough, since the plan expects many students to bike or take transit. The applicant's planner agreed to consider increasing the number.

The applicant's planner said the reduced parking reflects low parking use in the first phase and the developer's experience with other student buildings. The planner also said the angular plane relief applies only to one corner next to an institutional property.
